messages:
tina: noticed an oddness with async stream_tool_call when using function/tool outputs. sometimes yields strings, sometimes dicts — downstream pydantic models fail.

joel: do you have a tiny repro? streaming only or regular call_tool too?

tina: streaming only. non-streaming call_tool always returns parsed dicts. repro: 
```
async for chunk in client.stream_tool_call(model="gptx-tool", tool="parse_struct", input=prompt):
    print(type(chunk))
```

tina: sample yields: 
1) '"{\\\"id\\\": 1, \"data\\\": ' 
2) '{\"id\": 1, \"data\": {\"x\": 2}}'

marco: sounds like chunk boundary split through JSON token. our streaming parser currently tries json.loads per chunk. we should buffer until a complete object is available.

joel: constraint: we do want to surface partial text sometimes for debug and low-latency consumers. proposal: default behavior = yield parsed objects only; provide opt-in raw frame stream via client.stream_tool_call(raw=True).

marco: +1. also add typed API: stream_tool_call[T](model, tool, ...) -> AsyncIterator[T] where T is pydantic model. SDK does incremental buffer + validate with T.parse_raw. simplifies user code and fixes mypy.

tina: that would be ideal. current workaround is gross (user-side buffer + json.loads).

bot-ci: linked CI flake: https://ci.redwood/5678/streaming-split-json (failing tests)

joel: action items:
- fix: incremental buffer in streaming handler so we only json.loads when complete object arrives (high)
- add raw=True debug mode that emits every transport frame (low)
- design typed streaming API using pydantic + typing aliases (medium)
- add unit tests that split JSON at arbitrary byte boundaries and simulate reconnects (high)

marco: I'll take the buffer + tests. joel, can you draft the typed API surface? I'll ensure reconnect resets are correct (don't drop half objects).

tina: thanks—i'll add repro snippet + logs to GH issue and tag you both.

joel: for changelog, note that until fix lands callers may see str frames; encourage non-streaming call_tool for applications that rely on strict typed outputs.

marco: planning patch for next minor release.
